chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

'We are a people whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has made obedience to us obligatory. For us are the anfal (spoils of war), and for us is the choicest of wealth, and we are the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, and we are the envied ones about whom God said:
"Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His grace?"

key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: Al-Rasikhun fil-'Ilm — 'those deeply rooted in knowledge'; a Quranic phrase from 3:7 referring to those who fully comprehend the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) of the Quran. Shia theology identifies the Imams as these persons.
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: Anfal — literally 'the extra gains', referring to properties and wealth not specifically allocated by conventional division of spoils: uncultivated lands, coastal areas, riches of kings, etc. In Shia theology, these belong to the Imam.
key_terms.الْمَحْسُودُونَ: Al-mahsudun — 'the envied ones'; the Imam claims this Quranic description (4:54) refers to the Ahl al-Bayt who were envied for the divine gifts bestowed upon them.
key_terms.صَفْوُ الْمَالِ: Safwa al-mal — 'the choicest/purest part of wealth'; the best portion of any property or estate, which the Imam has a right to take.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Ahlulbayt being the rasikhun in knowledge and the recipients of the anfal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserts the divine authority of the Ahlulbayt by identifying them as the community whose obedience has been made obligatory by God, the rightful recipients of the anfal and pure wealth, the Rasikhun fil-'Ilm (those deeply rooted in knowledge) referenced in the Quran, and the people described in Quran 4:54 as being envied for God's grace bestowed upon them. This hadith connects three distinct Quranic concepts — mandatory obedience, the anfal, and the 'rasikhun in knowledge' — to the Imamate, asserting them as exclusive attributes of the Ahl al-Bayt. The original Shia audience would have understood this as a doctrinal statement about the Imam's authority, particularly the claim to the anfal (Quran 8:1) which was a contested economic and theological issue in early Islam.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘We<sup>asws</sup> are a people, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Necessitated obedience to us<sup>asws</sup>. For us<sup>asws</sup> are the spoils of war, and for us<sup>asws</sup> is the clean wealth, and we<sup>asws</sup> are the ones deeply rooted in the knowledge, and we<sup>asws</sup> are the envied ones for whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Said
[4:54] Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His grace?’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ibn ‘Umayr from abu al-Sabah al-Kinani who has said that Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“We are a people obedience to whom is obligatory by the command of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. The Anfal (twenty percent in tax) is for us and we have been given the authority to choose the best out of the property seized from the enemy. We are the people very firmly established in knowledge. We are the ones who are considered as subject to the jealousy of people in the following verse of the holy Quran,
“Are they jealous of the favors that God has done to some people? . [4:54]
